note: Static candidates from /vuln-scan. Confidence is scanner self-reported; /triage performs the rigorous N-vote verification. F-rag-iso-02 and a duplicate source_url finding were merged into F-rag-pii-02; a ReDoS negative-result note was dropped.

findings.title: No size cap on ingest raw_content/text enables embedding-cost inflation (T9)
findings.description: IngestRequestSchema.raw_content is z.string().min(1) with no .max(); same gap in reference-ingest.ts:15 and itinerary-ingest.ts:28. reference/itinerary content flows straight into embedWithUsage → OpenAI embeddings.create with no per-request token/byte ceiling or batch cap. /api/ingest queues to pending_review (no embed until approval), so the direct-embed cost path is the platform-admin-scoped reference+itinerary routes.
findings.exploit_scenario: A write-scoped (or platform-admin) caller submits multi-MB text bodies in a loop; each is embedded at per-token OpenAI cost with no cap, inflating OPENAI_API_KEY spend.
findings.recommendation: Add .max(N) (~32-50KB, aligned to the embedding token window) to raw_content/text in all three ingest schemas and a hard per-request/per-batch char cap before embed(); reject oversized with 413/422.

findings.title: Feedback rate-limit runs before HMAC verification; spoofable bucket, pre-auth Redis writes
findings.description: checkFeedbackRateLimit runs at line 60 BEFORE the HMAC compare (lines 68-73). The key is rl:feedback:${remote}:${secretHint} where remote is the attacker-controlled x-forwarded-for and secretHint is a server-side constant. So (1) every unauthenticated POST executes redis.incr (a write) pre-auth, and (2) an attacker setting x-forwarded-for to the main app's egress IP shares the legit caller's 120/min bucket and can exhaust it — all without a valid signature.
findings.exploit_scenario: Attacker learns the main app's egress IP and sends 120 unsigned POSTs/min with X-Forwarded-For:<egress-ip> and junk signature; each is rejected only AFTER the rate-limit increment, exhausting the shared bucket so genuine signed feedback gets 429'd — suppressing ranking signal without the secret.
findings.recommendation: Verify the HMAC FIRST, then rate-limit only authenticated requests. Drop the constant secretHint from the key; don't derive the bucket solely from the spoofable forwarded-for header.

findings.title: source_url/image_url accept file:// and internal-host schemes, stored verbatim and returned at retrieval (T8)
findings.description: source_url is z.string().url().optional() (also reference-ingest.ts:16, itinerary-ingest.ts:27, approve.ts:14; image_url/source_page_url in media-asset-upsert.ts:11-12). zod .url() validates via new URL() which accepts file://, ftp://, http://169.254.169.254, internal hosts — no scheme/host allowlist. Persisted verbatim and returned unmodified at retrieve/route.ts:210-211. RAG does not fetch it, but downstream clients/renderers do (client-side SSRF / internal probe / phishing citation). Merges the tenant-isolation agent's identical finding.
findings.exploit_scenario: A caller ingests source_url=file:///etc/passwd or image_url=http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/...; after approval the chunk/asset is retrieved and a downstream UI/img-proxy resolves the internal URL, exfiltrating internal data or presenting a phishing link as a citation.
findings.recommendation: Constrain the schema to an http/https allowlist and reject RFC1918/link-local/localhost/non-DNS hosts; re-validate at render time; never server-side-fetch a stored URL without the same allowlist.

findings.title: Captured valid feedback webhook can be replayed indefinitely to inflate ranking (no nonce/timestamp/idempotency)
findings.description: None of the three webhook routes include a signed timestamp or nonce, and there is no replay cache. /api/feedback inserts one new knowledge_chunk_feedback_events row per chunk on every accepted request with no source_revision/dedup (unlike tenant-events/platform-settings which have a monotonic stale-guard). The signature covers only the static body, so it stays valid forever; compute_feedback_factor reads these events at retrieval, steering ranking.
findings.exploit_scenario: An on-path observer or anyone who obtains one signed feedback body+signature replays it thousands of times; each replay adds up/down-vote events for the cited chunk_ids, promoting/demoting specific knowledge chunks the downstream LLM sees — without learning RAG_WEBHOOK_SECRET.
findings.recommendation: Add a signed timestamp + skew window and record a per-request nonce (or hash of message_id+chunk_ids+ts) in the existing Redis jti/replay cache so each event is accepted once; or give feedback events an idempotency key the insert dedups on.

findings.title: Retrieved chunk content returned verbatim with no untrusted-content tagging (T5)
findings.description: Chunks are returned with content: c.content and no wrapping/sentinel/untrusted flag distinguishing user/tenant-ingested free text from trusted data. The retrieve contract gives the downstream LLM caller no machine-readable provenance signal, so an 'ignore previous instructions' payload ingested into a tenant chunk surfaces indistinguishable from authoritative content. Partially RAG-owned (the contract could carry the flag) even though final enforcement is the caller's.
findings.exploit_scenario: A tenant-scoped ingest submits chunk content containing injection text; after approval it is retrieved and concatenated into the downstream LLM prompt with no untrusted marker, and the model follows the embedded instructions.
findings.recommendation: Add an explicit provenance/untrusted marker per returned chunk (e.g. untrusted: scope==='tenant' || source_type!=='scraped_reference') and document the wrapping requirement in the retrieve contract.

findings.title: Zero-tolerance PII prefilter false-negatives: alternate/no separators pass through (T4)
findings.description: SSN_PATTERN only allows [-\s] separators and intentionally excludes the no-separator form 123456789, so 123.45.6789 / 123456789 are not detected. CARD_CANDIDATE /\b(?:\d[ -]?){13,18}\d\b/ only tolerates space/hyphen, so dot-separated cards (4111.1111.1111.1111) are never Luhn candidates. Passport detection applies no separator stripping. These are real false-negatives for the categories the gate claims to guarantee.
findings.exploit_scenario: A submitter includes an SSN as 123.45.6789 or a dot-separated card; the prefilter returns detected:false, the content skips quarantine, is approved, embedded, and returned verbatim — defeating the zero-tolerance guarantee.
findings.recommendation: Normalize input (strip [\s.\-] into a digits-only view) and run Luhn/SSN structural checks on it in addition to formatted patterns; add fixtures for dotted/unseparated forms.

findings.title: feedback route uses a hand-rolled string timingSafeEqual with early length-return
findings.description: The feedback route defines its own timingSafeEqual(a,b) that returns false immediately on length mismatch and otherwise XOR-accumulates char codes, unlike tenant-events/platform-settings which use node crypto.timingSafeEqual over Buffers. The early length return leaks length (expected is a known fixed 64-hex, so minimal) and a hand-rolled comparator is more fragile.
findings.exploit_scenario: Marginal: timing could distinguish wrong-length from right-length-wrong-bytes, but since the expected length is publicly known this gives no real forging advantage. Reported for robustness/consistency.
findings.recommendation: Replace with crypto.timingSafeEqual(Buffer.from(provided),Buffer.from(expected)) guarded by a length check, matching the other two routes.

findings.title: Primary vector-retrieval path is DB-only single-layer (no JS re-filter), unlike every other chunk path
findings.description: The route's documented two-layer property (DB .or() + JS re-filter) is enforced for asset re-queries and the structured itinerary/ship/port lookups, but the primary match_knowledge_chunks RPC result flows to the response with NO JS scope/tenant re-filter — isolation rests entirely on the RPC's WHERE (scope='global' OR tenant_id=p_tenant_id). Correct today (p_tenant_id bound to ctx), but the one critical path lacks the app-layer backstop, so a future RPC refactor could leak cross-tenant undetected.
findings.exploit_scenario: No direct exploit. An engineer edits the multi-CTE match_knowledge_chunks (which already needed search_path/two-phase fixes) and weakens the scope predicate in one branch; the main vector path silently returns tenant B's chunks to tenant A while the helper paths' JS filters would have caught it.
findings.recommendation: Apply the same JS re-filter to vectorRows: drop rows where row.scope==='tenant' && row.tenant_id!==ctx.tenant_id before merging (RPC already returns scope and tenant_id).

findings.title: Service JWT verified without audience or issuer binding
findings.description: jwtVerify is called with only { algorithms: ['RS256'] } — no audience or issuer; the signer sets neither aud nor iss. RAG accepts ANY RS256 token signed with the service keypair, for any tenant_id in tenant_registry_shadow and any service_identifier including platform-admin. No defense-in-depth if the keypair is reused for another service or a main-app path lets an attacker influence the claims.
findings.exploit_scenario: An attacker who obtains any token-minting capability in main (a future endpoint signing a service JWT with partly user-controlled service_identifier, or key reuse) presents it to RAG admin routes; with no aud/iss to reject it, it reaches the platform-admin gate.
findings.recommendation: Add audience ('atc-rag') and issuer ('atc-main') to both SignJWT (setAudience/setIssuer) and jwtVerify options; update the check-sequence comment.

findings.title: Destructive admin routes gate on service_identifier but not write scope
findings.description: purge-tenant-scoped-chunks, demote-chunk, post-termination-mark, post-termination-review, set-authority-override check service_identifier==='platform-admin' but NOT ctx.scope==='write' (only replace-chunk, tenant-chunk-counts, media-assets/upsert assert scope). scope (read|write) is set independently of service_identifier by the signer, so a read-scoped platform-admin token can perform deletes.
findings.exploit_scenario: A platform-admin token minted scope:'read' for a read-only admin op is replayed/misused against purge-tenant-scoped-chunks and deletes tenant chunks, because the route never checks scope.
findings.recommendation: Add `if (ctx.scope !== 'write') return 403` to the mutating admin routes, matching replace-chunk:34; pin with a test asserting a read-scoped platform-admin token is rejected.
